name: Hemoglobin Lepore Beta-Thalassemia Intermedia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Hematological Diagnostic Criteria for Beta-Thalassemia Intermedia

criteria.description: Identification of Hb Lepore fusion gene combined with beta-thalassemia mutations by molecular genetic testing
Chronic anemia with hemoglobin levels typically between 7 and 10 g/dL without regular transfusion dependence
Presence of Hb Lepore variant on hemoglobin electrophoresis or HPLC with elevated HbF and reduced HbA
Mild to moderate splenomegaly and extramedullary hematopoiesis without severe transfusion requirement
Evidence of ineffective erythropoiesis and marrow expansion on bone marrow biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of Hb Lepore fusion gene with beta-thalassemia mutations plus characteristic hemoglobin electrophoresis findings and chronic anemia consistent with intermedia phenotype
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of genetic, hematological, and clinical data to distinguish from beta-thalassemia major and minor.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of Hemoglobin Lepore variant on electrophoresis
searchTerms: presence of Hb Lepore on electrophoresis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic mild to moderate anemia (hemoglobin 7-10 g/dL)

searchTerms: enlarged spleen from blood cell production
spleen swelling due to extra blood cell formation
spleen enlargement caused by blood cell growth outside marrow

common.symptomName: Bone deformities due to marrow expansion
searchTerms: bone deformities due to increased marrow activity
abnormal bone shape from marrow growth
yellowing of skin from red cell breakdown
skin and eye yellowing due to destroyed red cells
chronic fatigue due to low red blood cells
gallstones caused by chronic red cell breakdown

occasional.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias due to iron overload
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems due to excess iron

laboratory: Elevated HbF and presence of Hb Lepore on hemoglobin electrophoresis or HPLC
Elevated serum ferritin in some cases due to iron overload
imaging: Bone marrow expansion visible on skull and long bone X-rays
Splenomegaly and hepatomegaly on abdominal ultrasound
genetic: Co-inheritance of beta-thalassemia mutations confirmed by molecular analysis
other: Bone marrow biopsy showing erythroid hyperplasia and ineffective erythropoiesis

distinguishingFeatures: More severe anemia requiring regular transfusions
Normal or slightly elevated HbA2 without Hb Lepore
No significant splenomegaly or bone deformities
Presence of HbE variant instead of Hb Lepore

redFlags: Signs of iron overload despite minimal transfusions
